tex_content.html:
Corollary
↗ thm:quotient-manifold-theorem ↗ thm:group-action-riemannian-submersion 1. ch2:2.29

If a Lie group $G$ acts smoothly, freely, properly, and isometrically on $(\tilde M,\tilde g)$, then $\tilde M/G$ has a unique smooth manifold structure and Riemannian metric for which the quotient map is a Riemannian submersion.

Proof

\sketch The quotient manifold theorem gives the smooth structure and a smooth submersion quotient map. The action is vertical and fiber-transitive by definition, so Theorem 3 supplies the unique metric.

□
